questions.q: Name one way a river changes downstream.
questions.a: Wider, deeper, faster, more discharge, smaller and rounder sediment

questions.q: Calculate the cross-sectional area at site 3.
questions.model: Area = width × mean depth. 3.8 × 0.32 = 1.216. About 1.22 m².

questions.q: Describe the change in velocity downstream, using data.
questions.a: Increases from 0.20 m/s at 2 km to 0.50 m/s at 18 km
Deeper, wider channel has less friction relative to volume; more water from tributaries

questions.q: (c) Suggest one reason for the change in discharge.
(d) Explain one limitation of measuring velocity with a float.
questions.a: floats measure surface speed only, affected by wind
few sites, one day, surface velocity, judgement

questions.q: Self-mark with the mark scheme; add one target to your enquiry summary card.
Sketch the expected long profile for this river and label sites 1 to 5.
questions.a: A concave profile, steep near the source, gentle near site 5
